tool.name: FAIRe mapper: find method details
tool.description: propose FAIRe values for the laboratory and bioinformatic methods, for review
tool.command: #import re python '$__tool_directory__/faire_method_details.py' #for $t in $methods: '$t' #end for #for $t in $methods: #set $lab = $re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9._ ()-]', '_', str($t.element_identifier)) --label '$lab' #end for --checklist '$__tool_directory__/checklist/FAIRe_checklist_v1.0.2.xlsx' --assay_type '$assay_type' #if str($assay_names).strip(): --assay_names '$assay_names' #end if $whole_text --output '$proposals' --review_sheet '$review_sheet' > '$summary'

param.name: methods
param.label: Methods
param.help: The methods of the study as plain text, markdown or a PDF: a methods section, a whole paper, a report, or a README with methods. Give several files if the methods are spread over a paper and its supplement. A PDF of scanned pages holds pictures of the text, which the tool can't read: save it, or a Word file, as text first.

param.name: assay_names
param.label: Assay names (optional)
param.help: Separated by commas, as in your other files (Fish16S, COI_Leray). A value found in a sentence that names one of them is proposed for that assay. Leave empty if the study has one assay.

param.name: whole_text
param.label: Read the whole text
param.help: By default, a text with a Methods heading is read from that heading to the Results, Discussion or References heading, with any supplementary methods after the references. Other parts of a paper name tools and kits that other studies used. Choose this if the tool misses part of your methods.

has_text.text: the whole text (no Methods heading found)

tool.help:
@EARLY_VERSION@ **What it does**
Much of what FAIRe asks about a study is in its methods: how the water was filtered, the extraction kit, the PCR conditions, the sequencing instrument and kit, and the software, settings and reference databases of the bioinformatics. This tool reads the methods and proposes a value for each of these FAIRe terms it can recognise, with the sentence the value came from, so that you can check it. It writes a review sheet: you accept, reject or change each value, fill in what the tool did not find, and give the sheet to **FAIRe mapper: apply mapping** with your other values for the whole project.
The tool reads by rules, not with a language model, so it runs offline and gives the same answer each time. It knows the instruments, thermocyclers, master mixes, extraction kits, filters, software, pipelines and reference databases listed in its vocabulary, and the usual ways methods sections state a value, such as "40 cycles of 95 °C for 30 s", "in 25 µL reactions", "maximum expected errors = 2" or "a query coverage of 96%". It can miss values written in other ways, and it cannot tell which assay a value belongs to unless the sentence names it. Every value is a proposal for you to check.
Primers are left to **FAIRe mapper: find primers**, which looks them up in a table of published primers.
-----
**Inputs**
- **Methods**: plain text, markdown or a PDF. When the text is a whole paper, the tool reads its Methods section, from the Methods heading to the Results, Discussion or References heading, and any supplementary methods after the references. The introduction and discussion name tools and kits that other studies used, so they are left out. - **Assay names** (optional): with two or more assays, a value in a sentence that names one of them is proposed for that assay.
**Outputs**
- **Review sheet** (Excel), with a *Method details* sheet and a *How to review* sheet. The first rows are the values found, each with the FAIRe term, what FAIRe asks for, the proposed value, the sentence it came from and how it was found. Choose a *Reviewer's decision* for each: Accept, Change (and write the right value in *Your value*) or Reject. When a term has several values (two storage temperatures, say), keep the one that applies to your eDNA samples. The rows after them are the FAIRe method terms the tool did not find: write a value in *Your value* for any you know. Rows with no decision and no value of your own are left out of the workbook. The sheet can be sorted and filtered. - **Values found** (tabular): the same values, one per line, with the section, term, value, assay, sentence, how it was found, a note and the status *review*. - **Summary**: what was read, and the terms found in each part of the methods.
**What it looks for**
- *Field and laboratory hygiene*: sentences about bleach, UV or other cleaning (sterilise_method). - *Sampling and filtration*: the sampling device; the volume collected and the volume filtered (samp_size and samp_vol_we_dna_ext, which people often mix up, so the note says how they differ); the filter's pore size, diameter, material and name; active or passive filtration; the sentence that describes the filtration; the storage temperature before filtering (samp_store_temp) and after it (prepped_samp_store_temp); what the samples were preserved in. - *DNA extraction*: the kit, how it lyses the cells and separates the DNA, the changes made to the kit's protocol, and any clean-up kit. - *PCR*: the PCR programme in the FAIRe format (initial denaturation:95_15;denaturation:95_0.5; annealing:54_1.5;elongation:72_1.5;final elongation:72_10;40), the annealing temperature and number of cycles, the reaction and template volumes, PCR replicates, the master mix or the reaction's own recipe, the thermocycler, and any test for inhibition. A second PCR that adds the indexes gives the pcr2 terms. - *Library preparation and sequencing*: one-step or two-step indexing, the instrument (with its OBI identifier where the tool knows it) and platform, the sequencing kit or flow cell, paired or single reads, the sequencing facility, and how the libraries were checked and pooled. - *Bioinformatics*: the software for each step (trimming, demultiplexing, merging, quality and length filtering, denoising or clustering, chimera removal, comparison with the reference) with its version and settings; the cut-offs (minimum length, expected errors or Phred score, overlap, mismatches, minimum reads, clustering threshold); the reference databases with their version or date; how the taxonomy was assigned and the identity and coverage thresholds; the lowest common ancestor step; and how taxa found in the controls, outside their range or outside the study's target were removed.
The vocabulary is a table, ``method_details/vocabulary.tsv`` beside the tool, which anyone can add rows to: an instrument, kit or program the tool does not know yet is one line.
